title: Canonical witness result — v1.0
description: The renderer-independent result a witness's `determinism.value_hash` is taken over. plan.md §16.1 states the split but not the artifact: 'the renderer does not currently emit a canonical numeric result separate from the SVG' -- this is that artifact (chainlink #27). Generated at ci/results/witnesses/<witness_id>.json; machine-emitted, no review block, for the same reason a C_static report carries none. THE FLOAT RULE, which is the whole reason this exists rather than hashing the SVG: a canonical result contains NO JSON NUMBERS FOR MEASURED VALUES. Every measured value is a decimal STRING in a constrained form, produced by whatever computed it. Hashing therefore never formats a float, and the fragility §16.1 names (float-to-string formatting, locale, rounding, attribute order, library version) cannot reach the normative hash: it is confined to the producer, where G19 (#30) catches it by regenerating. `value_domain` is recomputed from the values on every validation and rejected on disagreement -- the same computed-never-stored discipline G1b applies to eligibility in I and coverage in a C_static report -- so a degeneracy check (G20, #31) reading `distinct_values` is reading a fact, not a claim.

renderer_actual.description: What actually produced this result. Carried here as well as in the witness spec's `output` so a result file is self-describing: a result found on its own must still be able to say what made it, or a mismatch is only visible to whoever holds both files.

canonicalization.description: How value_hash was computed, recorded IN the artifact. A hash whose derivation is only documented in a script is unverifiable the moment the script changes; naming the rule and the hashed field set makes a future change visible as a version bump rather than as a silent re-hash.

rule.description: JSON, UTF-8, keys sorted, separators (',' ':') with no whitespace, no trailing newline, over exactly the fields named in hashed_fields. Implemented by scripts/witness_result.py.

hashed_fields.description: The identity of the fact, plus the fact. Deliberately excludes renderer_actual, value_domain, paths and anything else about HOW the value was obtained or displayed: the same numbers computed by a different renderer are the same fact and must hash the same, while the same numbers from a different fixture or seed are a different fact and must not.

value_domain.description: Recomputed from `result` on every validation and rejected on disagreement. Exists so a degeneracy check is a lookup rather than a re-derivation: `value_distribution: must-vary` fails exactly when distinct_values is 1 (G20, #31). minimum/maximum are compared as decimals, not as strings, and are absent-safe only for an empty result, which the result kinds forbid.

value_hash.description: Over the canonical serialization of hashed_fields. Recomputed by scripts/witness_result.py and rejected on disagreement -- a stored hash is a claim, and this one is normative.

decimal.description: A measured value, as a canonical decimal string. NOT a JSON number: a JSON number would have to be re-formatted to be hashed, and that formatting step is precisely the platform-dependent thing §16.1 says must not reach the normative hash. The producer emits this form (scripts/witness_result.py's canonical_number() is the reference implementation: shortest round-trip for f64, normalized exponent, no '+', no leading zeros, a single spelling of zero, and no trailing zeros in the fraction -- 0.10 and 0.1 are one number and must never be two hashes). NaN and ±Infinity have no spelling here at all -- a witness whose value is not a number has no stable value to pin, and the schema refuses to give it one.

result.description: Three kinds, covering the renderer families §16.1 names: a single value, a keyed sequence, and a 2-D field (what scalar_field_svg draws and what `coverage_region` talks about). Adding a fourth is a reviewed schema change like any other -- the closed set is what stops a producer inventing a shape the gates cannot read.

points.description: Order is significant and is part of the hash: a series reordered is a different serialization, and a producer that emits points in a nondeterministic order has a determinism defect G19 should catch rather than a canonicalizer should hide.

cells.description: Sparse by design: a feature defined only along a corridor or a bottom row has cells only there, which is what makes `coverage_region` a checkable statement about the result rather than about the picture. Cells are required to be unique by (row, column) and sorted (scripts/validate_witness.py) -- two values for one cell has no meaning, and an unsorted order would make the hash depend on iteration order.
